mechanism.description: Persistent hyperkalemia or large potassium variability (often from CKD or RAAS blockade) increases arrhythmia susceptibility. Hypoglycemia-induced sympathoadrenal activation can precipitate arrhythmias; their combination could increase harm under intensive therapy.

Potassium is a surrogate for CKD severity and RAAS inhibitor exposure; CKD modifies hypoglycemia risk, drug handling, and CV risk composition, so the potassium signal may reflect underlying renal disease rather than a direct potassium effect.

Some glucose-lowering therapies or their dosing adjustments in CKD alter hypoglycemia risk and potassium handling (e.g., insulin shifts), but direct pharmacologic interactions with potassium are secondary and require precise data to support.
